title: Weather watching
intro: The weather is always doing something. Ten cards for noticing it. Take what you like.

cards.front: Which way are the clouds moving?
cards.back: Pick a cloud and follow it for a few seconds. See whether it moves quickly or drifts slowly.
Try to name the colour in your own words. Is it nearer white, blue or grey, or something in between?
Look at trees, flags or loose leaves for clues. Or open a window and feel the air.

cards.front: How does the light fall today?
cards.back: Notice whether shadows are sharp or soft, and which way they point.
Rain, cut grass, warm pavement and cold air can all smell different.

cards.front: What would you wear outside right now?
cards.back: A thought experiment is enough. No need to go and get the coat.

cards.front: Find the highest cloud you can see
cards.back: High clouds often look thin and wispy. Lower ones usually look thicker and darker.
Wind, rain and even a very still day each have a sound of their own.

cards.front: How is the weather different from yesterday?
cards.back: Even small changes in temperature or cloud count. If you do not remember, that is fine.

cards.front: Say the weather in one word
cards.back: Choose a word that feels right to you. It does not have to be the usual one.
